title: exFAT regrown holes expose the file's old backing bytes
mechanism: exFAT truncate frees clusters only in the allocation bitmap. A later extending write reallocates them first-fit, PageCache::resize zero-fills only the old partial tail page, and submit_read_bio returns zeros only for pages at or beyond logical size, so hole pages below EOF are read from the reused clusters' old on-disk bytes.
contract: lseek(2)/ftruncate(2): bytes in a gap created by writing or extending past EOF read as zeros until written.
observed: After ftruncate(fd, 0) and a pwrite of one page at 8192 on exFAT, pread of [0, 8192) returned the file's previous 'A' and 'B' page contents instead of zeros.

repro.how_to_run: Build both C files statically, pack them as /init and /test_mc5 in a cpio, attach fresh ext2 (/dev/vda) and exFAT (/dev/vdb, 4096-byte clusters) images, and boot. MC5_RESULT BUG on the [exfat] line means the bug fired.

caveats: Same-file stale data only. No cross-file or cross-principal disclosure was demonstrated. Deterministic reuse relies on a fresh image where the subject owns the lowest free clusters. ext2 and ramfs controls ran in the same guest. No Linux run was recorded.
